text:
I that please some, try all: both joy and terror
Of good and bad, that makes and unfolds error,
Now take upon me, in the name of Time,
To use my wings.
plain: Time tests everyone, brings the good and the bad, and slides past whatever you hoped would stay.

text:
I think affliction may subdue the cheek,
But not take in the mind.
plain: Hardship can wear down your face. It only gets your mind if you let it in.

text:
I am but sorry, not afeard; delay’d,
But nothing alt’red: what I was, I am:
More straining on for plucking back; not following
My leash unwillingly.
plain: Pulled back, not changed. The harder they yank the leash, the harder I pull forward.

text:
The selfsame sun that shines upon his court
Hides not his visage from our cottage, but
Looks on alike.
plain: The same sun shines on the palace and the shack. Power is not the same as worth.

text: Ha, ha! what a fool Honesty is! and Trust, his sworn brother, a very simple gentleman!
plain: This is how a con man sees honest people. Don't be the easy mark.

text: I see this is the time that the unjust man doth thrive.
plain: Sometimes the crooked one is winning. Don't confuse that with being right.

text:
As every present time doth boast itself
Above a better gone, so must thy grave
Give way to what’s seen now!
plain: Every era brags it beats the last one, and the past always gets pushed aside.

text:
Scarce any joy
Did ever so long live; no sorrow
But kill’d itself much sooner.
plain: Even joy rarely lasts that long, and no sorrow does. This will wear itself out.

text:
When I do count the clock that tells the time,
And see the brave day sunk in hideous night,
When I behold the violet past prime,
And sable curls all silvered o’er with white:
plain: Watch the clock long enough and you see everything beautiful going gray. Use the days.

text:
When I consider everything that grows
Holds in perfection but a little moment.
plain: Everything at its peak only holds it for a short moment.

text:
Shall I compare thee to a summer’s day?
Thou art more lovely and more temperate:
Rough winds do shake the darling buds of May,
And summer’s lease hath all too short a date:
plain: Even the best season is on a short lease. Good things end fast.

text:
So long as men can breathe or eyes can see,
So long lives this, and this gives life to thee.
plain: What you make and put into the world can outlive you.

text:
Yet do thy worst, old Time; despite thy wrong,
My love shall in my verse ever live young.
plain: Time will take everything, but not what I put into my work. Do your worst.

text:
The painful warrior famoused for fight,
After a thousand victories once foiled,
Is from the book of honour razed quite,
And all the rest forgot for which he toiled:
plain: A thousand wins get wiped out by one loss. Don't build your worth on the record.

text:
Yet in these thoughts my self almost despising,
Haply I think on thee, and then my state,
(Like to the lark at break of day arising
From sullen earth) sings hymns at heaven’s gate,
For thy sweet love remembered such wealth brings,
That then I scorn to change my state with kings.
plain: Low and full of self-hate, then one good thought lifts you and you wouldn't trade places with a king.

text:
When to the sessions of sweet silent thought,
I summon up remembrance of things past,
I sigh the lack of many a thing I sought,
And with old woes new wail my dear time’s waste:
plain: In quiet you count every wasted year and every old loss all over again.

text:
No more be grieved at that which thou hast done,
Roses have thorns, and silver fountains mud,
Clouds and eclipses stain both moon and sun,
And loathsome canker lives in sweetest bud.
plain: Everything good has something ugly in it. Stop beating yourself up for your flaws.

text:
Like as the waves make towards the pebbled shore,
So do our minutes hasten to their end,
Each changing place with that which goes before,
In sequent toil all forwards do contend.
plain: Minutes roll in like waves, each one pushing the last aside. They don't wait.

text:
This thought is as a death which cannot choose
But weep to have, that which it fears to lose.
plain: The more you love something, the more the fear of losing it eats at you.

text:
That time of year thou mayst in me behold,
When yellow leaves, or none, or few do hang
Upon those boughs which shake against the cold,
Bare ruined choirs, where late the sweet birds sang.
plain: Late in life, the branches are bare where the birds used to sing.

text:
Some glory in their birth, some in their skill,
Some in their wealth, some in their body’s force,
Some in their garments though new-fangled ill:
Some in their hawks and hounds, some in their horse.
plain: Everyone brags about something: family, money, muscle, clothes, toys.

text:
They that have power to hurt, and will do none,
That do not do the thing, they most do show,
Who moving others, are themselves as stone,
Unmoved, cold, and to temptation slow:
plain: The strongest people could hurt you and don't. They stay cold to temptation.

text:
Take heed (dear heart) of this large privilege,
The hardest knife ill-used doth lose his edge.
plain: Misuse a sharp gift and it dulls. Talent wasted on junk goes blunt.

text:
Let me not to the marriage of true minds
Admit impediments, love is not love
Which alters when it alteration finds,
Or bends with the remover to remove.
O no, it is an ever-fixed mark
That looks on tempests and is never shaken;
It is the star to every wand’ring bark,
Whose worth’s unknown, although his height be taken.
plain: Real love does not move when things change. It is the fixed star you steer by in a storm.

text:
O benefit of ill, now I find true
That better is, by evil still made better.
plain: Getting burned made the good thing better. Trouble can improve what you rebuild.
I know who I am. The ones judging me are often crooked themselves.

text:
Mad in pursuit and in possession so,
Had, having, and in quest, to have extreme,
A bliss in proof, and proved, a very woe;
Before a joy proposed behind a dream.
plain: Wanting it drives you mad, having it ruins you, and before you get it it was only a dream.

text:
Poor soul the centre of my sinful earth,
My sinful earth these rebel powers array,
Why dost thou pine within and suffer dearth
Painting thy outward walls so costly gay?
plain: You starve the part of you that matters while spending everything on the outside.

text:
So shall thou feed on death, that feeds on men,
And death once dead, there’s no more dying then.
plain: Live for what lasts and death loses its hold on you.

text:
Thus have I had thee as a dream doth flatter,
In sleep a king, but waking no such matter.
plain: It felt like a kingdom in the dream. Then you wake up and it is gone.
